newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Golden Vale says aims to improve profitability.
newsitem.headline: Golden Vale says aims to improve profitability.

text.p: Irish food company Golden Vale Plc said on Tuesday that its priorities for 1997 were to restore stability, improve profitability and to shape the future direction of the group.

"The group has been through an extremely difficult year which is reflected in the downturn in profits. In spite of this the group has generated a positive cash flow, and many of its businesses continue to perform well," Golden Vale said in a results statement.
"The priorities for 1997 are to restore stability, improve profitability and to shape the future direction of the group," it added.
Earlier, Golden Vale announced that its 1996 adjusted pre-tax profit had dropped to 7.9 million Irish pounds, before a 1.6 million punt charge, compared to 16.1 million a year earlier.

Turnover for the year was down to 561 million Irish pounds compared with 564 million punts in 1995 while operating profit before exceptional items was 12.1 million Irish pounds compared with 21.3 million punts previously.

Golden Vale said the reduction of 9.2 million punts in operating profit, before exceptional charges in 1996 was entirely due to the imbalance between milk price and weak market prices for butter and milk powders.
The group said in spite of the disappointing profit performance it had reduced its borrowings by 9.3 million Irish pounds in the year reducing gearing from 78 to 60 percent.
It said total debt now stood at 60.9 million punts and capital expenditure had been substantially maintained during the year at 7.3 million Irish pounds.

Golden Vale said turnover in its butter and milk products division in 1996 had fallen 2.3 percent to 252 million Irish pounds, operating profit had eased 11.7 million Irish pounds to 2.9 million punts while the margin on sales had dropped 4.5 percent to 1.2 percent.
"The fundamental problem behind the substantial decline in profits is the imbalance between milk prices for bulk butter and milk powders and the price paid for milk," it said.
It said selling prices had fallen by nine percent for bulk butter and seven percent for skim milk powder against 1995 compared to a fall in milk price of one percent.
The group said this margin pressure had been partially alleviated by higher sales volumes, improvement in retail butter margins and the continued development its added value powder business.

"Any improvement in performance in this business sector is clearly heavily dependent on absolute levels of milk price but is also dependent upon continuing the drive to add value to the basic products and to reduce the cost base of the business," it said.

Golden Vale said turnover in its cheese division had fallen by 2.4 percent to 123 million Irish pounds, operating profit was down 0.3 million punts to 0.8 million while the margin on sales had dropped 0.2 percent to 0.7 percent.

The group said the performance of the Dutch business from a 0.5 million Irish pounds contribution in 1995 to a negative contribution of 1.0 million punts in 1996 was a key factor behind the declines in the division.
It said the poor performance of the Dutch business was due to lower margins, volume loss and some one-off costs.
The launch costs of "Cheesestrings" in the British and Irish markets had totalled 2.5 million Irish pounds in 1996, the benefit from which would not come through in volume sales until 1997, it said.

It said the need to improve profits in the cheese business through the aggressive development of "Cheesestrings", continued expansion of the catering sector, the resolution of the issues at the Dutch subsidiary and improved performance in the retail sector was a key issue facing the company.

Golden Vale said turnover in its other businesses in Fluid Milks, Agri Trading, Spreads, Cream Liquers, UHT products and other sundry activities had risen by 3.3 percent to 186 million Irish pounds, operating profit had gained 2.8 million punts to 8.4 while the margin on sales was up 1.4 percent to 4.5 percent.
"Overall a very encouraging performance with steady growth in turnover and improved margins," Golden Vale said.
Golden Vale said the reduction of the overall cost base including significant improvements in manufacturing efficiency was a priority for the company in 1997.
"This is necessary in order to improve profitability and competitiveness in increasingly demanding food markets," it said.

It said it also aimed to maintain focus on product and customer development and to restore effective control of the administration of quota following the thorough examination of this area. --Dublin newsroom 353-1-661-3377
